title: Fusion Doc to JSON
summary: Builds Swami's Fusion Doc to JSON page: a browser tool that turns a zip of a saved Autodesk Fusion help page, plus its URL, into operation, tabs, sections and settings JSON for other dashboards.
what_it_is: A Claude skill that builds one **tool page**, not a report. The page is a vibe-dashboard with a Dashboard Summary, **Search**, **Input**, **Output**, a **JSON Format** table, a **Mind Map** and a **Glossary**, plus an audio overview. You drop in a zip of a saved Autodesk Fusion product-documentation page, confirm the page URL, and the page writes structured JSON: `operation > tabs > sections > settings`.

Everything runs in the viewer's browser; nothing is uploaded anywhere. The JSON feeds Swami's other Fusion dashboards, mainly the **fusion-cam-settings** skill, which matches each exported CAM setting to its Autodesk description. A published copy already exists; its byline shows its version, so Claude points Swami to it when it is current and rebuilds it to the same link when it isn't.
why: Autodesk's help pages explain every setting of a Fusion command, but only as a web page. Turning a page into JSON once lets other dashboards quote the official description next to each setting without copying text by hand.

what_it_does.text: Runs its own `build_page.py` straight on the vibe-dashboard template. It sets the sections, fills the Glossary, sets five categories (overview, input, output, format, reference), injects the converter script, and applies vibe-dashboard's table-fit, Search and Mind Map patches.
A built-in zip reader (no libraries) opens the upload in the browser, skips `__MACOSX/` and `._` files, and picks the `.html` that has a matching `_files` folder.
Takes the product documentation URL from the Input field, or else from the saved file's "saved from url" line or its canonical link.

Headings ending in "tab settings" start a tab. Headings that match the editable list of dialog group names start a section. Every other heading becomes a setting, with its description, notes, options (`Name - description` bullets), details, images and captions.
Sets `controlGuess` for each setting (dropdown, checkbox, selection, number or unknown) from its description.
Records each image by its file name, flags images the zip lacks, and can embed them as data URIs when that box is ticked.

Shows counts, a structure preview (tab, section, settings) and the JSON, with copy and download buttons. Download needs the artifact's downloads capability; without it the button hides and copy still works.
A table on the page lists every field the JSON holds, level by level, from the operation down to each setting's options and images.
Like every vibe-dashboard, the page has a Search section, a Mind Map, a 15-term Glossary and a spoken audio overview.
If Swami sends a zip in chat and wants the JSON now, Claude runs the page headlessly on it and sends `<operation>-settings.json`.

triggers: "Build the Fusion Doc to JSON page"
"Turn this saved Fusion help page into JSON" (with a zip)

how_to_use.step: Open the Fusion help page for the command or toolpath (for example Adaptive Clearing) in any browser that can save a complete page: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Comet, which Swami uses.
Use **File › Save Page As… › Webpage, Complete**. That writes an `.html` file and a `_files` folder of images.
In Finder, select the `.html` file and the `_files` folder, then right-click › **Compress 2 Items**.

Open the published Fusion Doc to JSON page and check the version in its byline. If it's out of date or you need it rebuilt, ask Claude, which builds it, records the audio, tests it, and republishes it to the same link with the downloads capability.
Drop the zip into Input, check the URL, and edit the dialog group names if a group is missing. The page converts as soon as the zip loads.
In Output, look over the structure preview. If settings sit in the wrong group, edit the group names and convert again.
Copy or download the JSON and give it to the next dashboard, such as fusion-cam-settings.

how_to_use_windows.step: In Edge, Chrome, Firefox or Comet, press **Ctrl+S** and choose **Webpage, Complete**. Files land in `C:\Users\<name>\Downloads` by default.
In File Explorer, select the `.html` file and the `_files` folder, then right-click › **Compress to ZIP file** (Windows 11) or **Send to › Compressed (zipped) folder** (Windows 10).
Open the same published page in Edge or Chrome; Input, Output, copy and download work the same as on the Mac.

capabilities.text: Converts entirely in the browser; the zip never leaves the computer.
Works on any Fusion help page saved as Webpage, Complete; tested on the Parallel Finishing page (5 tabs, 14 sections, 74 settings, 67 images).
The dialog group-name list is editable, so a wrong grouping can be fixed and converted again on the spot.
The published page is a lasting tool; it doesn't need rebuilding for each operation.
Search, the Mind Map and the Glossary make the page's instructions and JSON fields quick to find.

limitations.text: The help page doesn't say which dialog group a setting sits in, so sections come only from headings that match the group-name list. For example, Parallel's Leads and Transitions settings land in Linking.
Example values shown only in screenshots aren't extracted.
`controlGuess` is a guess from the description text.

gotchas.text: Save the page as **Webpage, Complete**, not HTML only, or the `_files` folder of images is missing. Safari has no such option (it saves a web archive), so use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Comet.
The zip must hold the `.html` file and its `_files` folder together.
If settings land in the wrong section, add the missing group name to the list in Input and convert again.
If neither the field nor the saved file gives a URL, the status line warns; add it and convert again.
The download button shows only when the page is published with the downloads capability; otherwise use copy.
The tool page's byline shows its version (v1.1.0 after this update). If your saved link shows an older one, ask Claude to republish it.
Unzipping needs `DecompressionStream`; a current Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox has it.
On Windows the saved page lands in `C:\Users\<name>\Downloads` unless you choose another folder.

requirements.text: A zip of one Fusion help page saved as Webpage, Complete, and ideally its URL.
Code execution ("Create and edit files") and artifacts, to build and publish the page.
A Mac (tested on macOS Tahoe), or a PC with Windows 10 or 11, with a browser that can save a complete page.

glossary.def: Autodesk's product-documentation web page for one Fusion command or toolpath.
The browser save option that writes the page's .html plus a _files folder of its images.
The folder of images the browser saves next to the .html file.
One compressed file holding the saved .html and its _files folder.
The web address of the help page, stored in the JSON so other dashboards can link to it.
The editable list of group headings that start a new section in the JSON.
A page of the Fusion dialog; a heading ending in "tab settings" starts one.
A dialog group inside a tab, such as Feed and Speed or Passes.
One control in the dialog, with its description, options, notes and images.
The parser's guess at a setting's control type: dropdown, checkbox, selection, number or unknown.
An image written into the JSON as text, so the JSON works without the zip.
The tab, section and settings outline shown in Output for a quick check.
The artifact permission that lets the page save the JSON as a file.
The skill's Python script that turns the vibe-dashboard template into the tool page and applies vibe-dashboard's patches.
The browser feature the page uses to unzip the upload without libraries.

spoken._intro: This page is the skill sheet for the Fusion doc to JSON skill. It builds a browser tool that turns a saved Autodesk Fusion help page into JSON for other dashboards
spoken.What It Is: What the skill is: one tool page, with input and output, a JSON format table, search, a mind map, a glossary and audio, that converts entirely in your browser
spoken.What It Does: Ten jobs, from building the page and reading the zip to parsing tabs, sections and settings, guessing control types, handling images, the output buttons, and the page's search, mind map, glossary and audio
spoken.How to Use It: Seven steps on the Mac, from saving the help page as webpage complete in a browser such as Comet and zipping it, to converting, checking the preview, and taking the JSON. Then three Windows steps
spoken.Skills It Depends On: Vibe dashboard is required for the template. Fusion cam settings and Fusion doc are related, because they use the JSON
spoken.Programs It Depends On: A browser and a zip tool on your computer, plus Python, a headless browser and the [Kokoro](/kˈoʊkoʊɹoʊ/) voice in Claude's workspace. Fusion itself isn't needed
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: It's private, works on any help page, lets you fix groupings on the spot, and is easy to search. But groups are guessed, dialog values aren't extracted, and control types are guesses
spoken.Scheduled Tasks: None. Its page is simply backed up each night with all the others
spoken.Where It Runs: Swami has run it in the desktop app linked to his MacBook Pro on macOS Tahoe. The other surfaces should work too, but are still untested
spoken.Gotchas: Eight traps, from saving the wrong page type, Safari included, and zipping only one file to missing groups, the download button, and checking the tool's version
spoken.Other Requirements: A zip of one help page, code execution and artifacts in Claude, and a Mac or Windows computer with a browser that can save a complete page
spoken.Card and Freshness: Which version of the skill this page describes, and its fingerprint. There are no open questions
